correctness.rationale: For surface-area-uniform independent points on sphere radius R>0, cutoff z in [-1,1), axial u uniform [z,1], azimuth uniform, gives E(U dot V)=((1+z)/2)^2 and E(U dot V)^2=tr(EUU^T)^2. Independent algebra verifies μ=R²(1-z)(z+3)/2 and ν=2R⁴(1-z)^2(z²+4z+5)/3. Thus κ=ν/μ²=(4/3)(1+t²), t=(1+z)/(3+z)∈[0,1/2), exactly feasible μ>0, 4/3<=κ<5/3. Inverse z=(3t-1)/(1-t) and R²=μ(1-t)²/(2(1-2t)). Cut-height estimate |Δz|<=2sqrt(3)|Δκ|^(1/2) is sharp by s=0,t↑1/2; angle exponent1/4 is sharp by full-sphere α→π, κ-4/3≈(π-α)^4/12. Analytic inequalities, not finite parameter samples, prove sharpness and universality.
